deals.evidence: un accord a été conclu pour le rachat par des investisseurs chinois et américains de 80% du capital du club
deals.headline: Chinese and American investors agree to buy 80% of OGC Nice
deals.investor: Chien Lee (NewCity Capital), Alex Zheng (Plateno Group) and Paul Conway (Pacific Media Group)
deals.seller: Gilbert Stellardo, Patrick Governatori, Jean Bessis and Louis Bacchialoni (49%) and Jean-Pierre Rivère (31% of his shares)
deals.summary: OGC Nice announced an agreement for Chinese and American investors to buy 80% of the club: the 49% held by Stellardo, Governatori, Bessis and Bacchialoni plus 31% from president Jean-Pierre Rivère, who kept 20%. The lead investors were Chien Lee (NewCity Capital) and Alex Zheng (Plateno Group), with Paul Conway (Pacific Media Group). No price was published.

deals.evidence: Ce dernier s’est engagé à prêter 22 millions d’euros au club niçois avec un taux d’intérêt de 9% remboursable sur quatre ans.
deals.headline: OGC Nice borrows EUR 22m at 9% from Luxembourg lender Thalos
deals.summary: Challenges reported that OGC Nice signed a four-year loan with Luxembourg credit fund Thalos Investment Platform (a subsidiary of Swiss group Vicenda) in late December 2018: EUR 22m at 9% interest, matching the sums the Sino-American owners had put into the club and wanted repaid.

deals.headline: INEOS completes the acquisition of OGC Nice
deals.seller: Chien Lee, Alex Zheng, Paul Conway and Jean-Pierre Rivère
deals.source_name: SportsPro (price and stake; completion date from the INEOS press release of 26 August 2019)
deals.summary: Jim Ratcliffe's INEOS completed the purchase of 100% of OGC Nice on 26 August 2019 after French competition clearance; the club joined INEOS Football (CEO Bob Ratcliffe). SportsPro, citing The Athletic, put the price at EUR 100m and INEOS's subsequent share capital injections at EUR 216m.

name: OGC Nice
notes: Revenue and P&L are the DNCG's published 2024/25 accounts (season to 30 June 2025, the latest the league has published; the 2025/26 accounts are due in spring 2027); the DNCG reports in thousands of euros, converted here to full units, and its perimeter is SASP OGC Nice + SARL Promofoot + Association. The same accounts show a EUR 48.05m profit on player transfers, a EUR 40.5m net loss, financial debts of EUR 5.98m and cash of EUR 62.2m at 30 June 2025 (no net-debt figure is stated, so none is recorded). No independent valuation (Forbes/Sportico) exists; the valuation field is the 2019 purchase price for 100%. INEOS put the club up for sale: SportsPro (May 2025, citing The Athletic) reported Lazard was hired and a EUR 250m asking price; Bloomberg (Jan 2026) reported a lower asking price; negotiations with a US investor failed on 12 June 2026 (Maxifoot, citing Nice-Matin) and INEOS kept the club. Sportune (30 Sep 2026) lists the 2019 purchase cost at EUR 100m. No attendance or social-follower figure with a date was found on a citable page.

owners.name: INEOS (INEOS Football; founder Jim Ratcliffe with co-owners Andy Currie and John Reece)

ownership_summary: OGC Nice (SASP Olympique Gymnaste Club de Nice Côte d'Azur) has been 100% owned by INEOS, Jim Ratcliffe's chemicals group, through its INEOS Football arm since 26 August 2019; the club names Ratcliffe and co-owners Andy Currie and John Reece. INEOS ran a sale process (Lazard was reported as adviser in May 2025), but talks with a US investor collapsed in June 2026 and INEOS kept the club.
